title: Selangor to explore additional aid for flood-hit hawkers, petty traders - The Edge Malaysia
text:
Selangor to explore additional aid for flood-hit hawkers, petty traders Monday 16 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google SHAH ALAM (Nov 16): The Selangor government will explore possible assistance for hawkers and petty traders affected by floods to help ease their financial burden.
 Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state administration was prepared to assist those affected, particularly in Kuala Selangor, where several areas are still experiencing stagnant floodwaters.
 He said the state government would first gather detailed information and data on the number of affected traders before determining the appropriate form of assistance.
 “We will assess the specific needs of the traders, as some may find that a one-off aid payment of RM500, RM1,000 or RM2,000 is insufficient, depending on the extent of their losses.
 “Therefore, we may consider alternative forms of assistance to help ease their financial burden and monthly commitments, particularly for petty hawkers,” he said.
 He was speaking to reporters after closing the 2026 state-level Hawkers and Petty Traders Day (HPPKS) at Dataran Kemerdekaan Shah Alam on Sunday (Nov 15) night.
 Also present were State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Najwan Halimi; Deputy State Secretary (Development)-cum-State Economic Planning Unit (UPEN) director Datuk Johary Anuar; and Selangor Menteri Besar Incorporated (MBI) chief executive officer Datuk Saipolyazan M Yusop.
 Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government would prioritise the distribution of financial assistance to flood victims, in line with aid announced earlier by the federal and state governments.
 “Our responsibility is to ensure that assistance reaches the heads of households as quickly as possible, including the additional RM500 announced by the Selangor state government.
 “There are two categories of recipients, those who registered and sought shelter at temporary evacuation centres, and those who did not,” he said.
 On HPPKS 2026, Amirudin said the two-day event attracted 15,000 visitors and generated nearly RM200,000 in sales.
 He said the event, organised by the state government's Standing Committee on Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship in collaboration with MBI, served as a platform to empower micro-entrepreneurs by providing marketing opportunities, exposure to digital technology and avenues for business networking.
 Now in its second year, the event recorded an increase in both visitor numbers and sales, supported by initiatives such as Platform Selangor (PLATS) and the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA), he added.
